questiontext.text:
Perpendicular Lines and Gradients

Consider the line L1 passing through the point \(({@x0@}, {@y0@})\) with gradient \({@m1@}\). A second line L2 passes through the same point and is perpendicular to L1.

Task. What is the gradient of L2?

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-10, 10, 10, -10], axis: true, showCopyright: false }); // Fixed point A (shared by both lines) var A = board.create('point', [{@x0@}, {@y0@}], {name: 'A', fixed: true, size: 3}); // Line L1 through A with slope m1: use a second point one unit to the right var P1 = board.create('point', [{@x0@}+1, {@y0@}+({@m1@})*1], {visible: false}); var L1 = board.create('line', [A, P1], {strokeWidth: 3}); // Perpendicular line L2 through A with slope m2 var P2 = board.create('point', [{@x0@}+1, {@y0@}+({@m2@})*1], {visible: false}); var L2 = board.create('line', [A, P2], {strokeWidth: 3, dash: 2}); // Labels board.create('text', [{@x0@}+0.3, {@y0@}+0.5, function(){ return "A"; }]); board.create('text', [-9.5, 9.2, function(){ return "Blue: L₁ (slope = {@m1@})"; }]); board.create('text', [-9.5, 8.4, function(){ return "Dashed: L₂ (perpendicular)"; }]); [[/jsxgraph]]

Answer:

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Tip: Perpendicular lines have gradients whose product is \(-1\).

generalfeedback.text:
Key fact: If two non-vertical lines are perpendicular, then their gradients multiply to \(-1\).
Here \(m_1 = {@m1@}\). Therefore the gradient of the perpendicular line is \[ m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1} = {@m2@}. \]
In the diagram: - The solid blue line is \(L_1\) with slope \({@m1@}\). - The dashed line is \(L_2\), perpendicular to \(L_1\). - They meet at the point \(({@x0@}, {@y0@})\).
